editorial:
Rachel Watson rides the same train every day, staring out the window at a house where a seemingly perfect couple lives. After her divorce, she drinks heavily and struggles with blackouts, but she still clings to this fantasy life she watches from afar. One morning she sees something disturbing at that house, and soon a woman goes missing. Because Rachel was nearby that night but cannot remember what happened, she becomes both a suspect and an unlikely investigator. The story pulls you into her messy, unreliable mind as she tries to piece together the truth.

Emily Blunt carries the whole movie with a raw, emotional performance that makes Rachel feel real even when she is frustrating. The pacing keeps you guessing, and the twists land well if you enjoy dark mysteries. Some scenes feel a bit slow, and the story can be confusing early on, but it rewards your patience. If you like psychological thrillers with unreliable narrators, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Rachel finally remembers the night Megan disappeared. She realizes her ex-husband Tom was having an affair with Megan and killed her to keep his secrets. Rachel confronts Tom at his home, and when he attacks her, Anna, his current wife, helps Rachel fight back. Rachel kills Tom with a corkscrew. The two women agree to tell police it was self-defense. Rachel finally gets closure and moves forward with her life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and unreliable narrators.
